findings.evidence: "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" vs. "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period"
findings.fix: Consolidate into one consistent statement specifying the publisher and publication frequency.
findings.location: Program Overview, first paragraph and Overview section
findings.violation: The document contradicts itself about how often the reimbursement log is published and which team publishes it.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph entirely or replace it with the actual standard approval timeline.
findings.violation: This describes a specific incident or workflow breakdown rather than a standard policy procedure and does not belong in a policy document.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the manager must follow the standard review checklist or has discretion to override it.
findings.violation: This statement contradicts the Approval Timeline section by suggesting the manager can disregard the standard checklist, creating ambiguity about what process actually governs approval.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.fix: Delete the second sentence or replace it with a meaningful statement if additional information is needed.
findings.violation: The sentence is redundant - reimbursement by definition offsets already-paid costs - and uses awkward phrasing.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite consistently, either "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and must be prepared for a brief photo check once per year" or use third-person throughout.
findings.violation: The sentence shifts inconsistently from direct address to the employer's perspective (you/we), creating confusing tone.

findings.evidence: Section contains descriptions of processes (how items are recorded and tracked) rather than definitions of terms.
findings.fix: Either rename the section to reflect its actual content (e.g., "Request Processing") or move the material to the appropriate section.
findings.violation: The section title promises terminology definitions but delivers process descriptions.

findings.evidence: "Program Overview" section near the beginning; "Overview" section appears later, containing overlapping content about the reimbursement log.
findings.fix: Consolidate the two sections into one Overview section placed at the document's beginning.
findings.violation: The document contains duplicate Overview sections that cover similar information.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either expand this section to list all steps in sequence, or merge it into the How to Apply section and remove this redundant heading.
findings.violation: The section heading implies multiple steps will be listed, but only one incomplete step is provided; the How to Apply section is more detailed.

findings.evidence: "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list."
findings.fix: Either include the approved equipment list in the policy or reference where employees can find it.
findings.violation: The policy references an "approved list" of equipment categories but never defines or provides this list.
